minutes.headline: Assessors heard the revaluation process from Vision and voted on the 2025 overlay recommendation; the vote count is not captioned.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors, with the Select Board attending, heard Vision's consultant explain how the preliminary FY24 revaluation values were built and the percent changes by class, style and neighborhood. They discussed public disclosure timing and outreach, then debated the recommended overlay figure for FY25 and voted on a motion for the lower of two proposed figures. Two additional meetings were planned to review abatement-adjusted residential values and commercial values.

public_comment.topic: Asked what base the assessment side of the assessment-to-sales ratio will use for lakefront properties, whether good/average/below-average classifications carry forward, and what base adjustments apply to.
Asked when residents get the 2024 assessment data and a public meeting, and asked that residents be allowed to ask questions.
Asked to put questions to the consultant; told to submit written questions to the town.

votes.motion: Select Board to adjourn its portion of the meeting (roll call)
Accept 120,000 as the overlay recommendation for the next fiscal year

budget_items.what_was_said: Consultant said the base land curve got a positive adjustment, and residual and undevelopable land rates were adjusted.
Building costs were raised from the prior year's range to low 150s, roughly an 8 to 10% increase.
Overall values rose, with condos and apartments up far more and waterfront neighborhoods down, measured against unabated 2023 values.

budget_items.topic: Share of homes with large changes
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member estimated some homes decreased and about a fifth rose by more than a tenth, implying an abatement workload.
Five-year average abatements were skewed by last year's large abatement event; normal years were far lower.
The town accountant said the FY24 overlay is already set, and the current cumulative balance was stated.
A board member proposed lowering the eligibility age and raising the allowance for seniors, which would require raising other exemptions and a town meeting vote.
A board member questioned why FY25 local receipt estimates fell in several categories.

budget_items.topic: Source of last year's abatement payout
budget_items.what_was_said: The town accountant said the large abatement amount was paid from free cash.
Members debated 120, 130-140 and 200 thousand for the FY25 overlay; a motion for the lowest was seconded.

decisions.decision: Reena will keep the assessor's office open every weekday from 8 to 4 until about the end of May to handle abatements.
Public questions for the consultant are to be submitted in writing, sent to the town, and passed to Vision rather than answered at this working meeting.
Board will send commercial and other questions to Mike by email, with a Zoom follow-up only if needed.
Board will look into costs of raising senior, veteran and blind exemptions and possibly draft a warrant article.
Chair will try to set public meetings for February 12 and February 15 at 6:30 for abatement-adjusted residential analysis, residential approval and commercial review.
Second-homeowner impact notice will go on the February 12 agenda.
Staff will build a visual sales board and a how-to-read-your-Vision-card guide, and place street listings at the library and senior center.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors heard Vision's consultant explain how preliminary revaluation values were built, with percent changes by class, style and neighborhood.
The board debated the recommended overlay for the next fiscal year and a motion for the lowest of the proposed figures was seconded; the captions do not make the vote outcome audible.
Public questions for the consultant are to be submitted in writing to the town and passed to Vision, not answered at this working meeting.
The board will look into the cost of raising senior, veteran and blind exemptions and possibly draft a warrant article.
The chair will try to set two public meetings for abatement-adjusted residential values and commercial review, and the second-homeowner impact notice goes on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: The preliminary values and the overlay, the reserve held for abatements, feed into what property owners are assessed and how much abatement money the town has set aside.
Any change to senior, veteran or blind exemptions would need a town meeting vote, so residents may be asked to vote on a warrant article.

The February 12 agenda, which is to carry the second-homeowner impact notice.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the $120,000 overlay figure, the $562,500 balance and the office hours, but they differ on the wording of the vote and on much of the surrounding detail. The thing to know: the official minutes record the overlay vote as a passed motion for the 2025 budget, ours has the outcome as inaudible, and the official minutes omit the follow-up decisions and meeting dates that ours records.
